doc.title: Bob Schulz interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Working musicians and the festival scene
title: Making a living as a musician
summary: Musicians joke their wives earn more; touring strains family life.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Oh that’s right. Oh man. So you can make between playing with the trad festivals and these kind of festivals, you can actually make a living as a musician — do you do other things?
Are you saying that with a straight face?
No. The talk with other musicians is, “I’ll bet my wife makes more money than yours.”
And my wife does make more money than I. She’s a manager, a property manager. But she’s very supportive and into it so—

Yeah I know. Unless you want to maintain a family life you just can’t just go out — in order to make a good living you have to be gone all the time. And then you can’t stay married. As it is she doesn’t like me going as much as I do, neither does my twelve year old.
